vulnerability.name: GHSA-qwgh-2vcv-g2f7
vulnerability.description: block-buffer: a panic caught inside a compression or block-generation callback leaves the cursor stored in the buffer's block out of bounds

statements.impact_statement: block-buffer 0.10.4 is in Cargo.lock and crates/agentd/fuzz/Cargo.lock only through digest 0.10.7, under blake2 0.10.6 and sha2 0.10.9 (snow) and sha1 0.10.7 (aws-config, axum, tungstenite); `cargo tree -i block-buffer@0.10.4 --target all` lists them. The 0.12.1 copy in Cargo.lock is the fixed release. The advisory's corruption needs the cursor to live inside the data block: 0.12.0's EagerBuffer keeps it in the block's last byte and its ReadBuffer in byte 0, so input copied in before a panicking callback overwrites it. 0.10.4 keeps the cursor in its own `pos: u8` field (src/lib.rs:61-62), which only `set_pos_unchecked` writes, after each callback returns (`digest_blocks`, `set_data`, `digest_pad`), and it has no ReadBuffer, so a caught panic leaves the previous, valid position. The advisory's EagerBuffer proof of concept, built in debug mode against both releases on 2026-10-27, read cursor 2 after the caught panic on 0.10.4 and failed the cursor invariant on 0.12.0. Re-check if either lockfile gains block-buffer 0.11.x or 0.12.0, if a 0.10.x release moves the cursor into the block, or if the advisory names a 0.10 code path.
statements.status_notes: Since 2026-10-30 GitHub and osv.dev list GHSA-qwgh-2vcv-g2f7's affected range as >= 0.11.0, < 0.12.1, so no scanner matches block-buffer 0.10.4 and the root and crates/agentd/fuzz osv-scanner.toml files no longer ignore it. The statement stays as the record of the 2026-10-27 analysis, which still holds for 0.10.4.

vulnerability.name: GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249
vulnerability.description: minimatch: at optimizationLevel 2 or above, a pattern's `**/../` segments multiply its glob parts during preprocessing, and the pairwise pass over them then takes quadratic time

statements.impact_statement: minimatch 10.2.6 is in site/pnpm-lock.yaml only, required as ^10.2.5 by typedoc 0.28.20 (also reached through typedoc-plugin-markdown 4.13.1), the docs site's devDependency that renders the TypeScript SDK reference from site/scripts/reference/sdk/typescript.mjs; `pnpm why minimatch` in site/ lists that one path, and nothing in site/ ships in a crate, wheel or npm package. The advisory's growth happens in firstPhasePreProcess and secondPhasePreProcess, which minimatch calls only when a caller sets optimizationLevel to 2 or more (dist/esm/index.js:332-341; the default is 1). typedoc builds every Minimatch with `{ dot: true }` or no options (dist/node-utils.js:62, :83 and :318), and `grep -rl optimizationLevel` over the dist directories of typedoc 0.28.20 and typedoc-plugin-markdown 4.13.1 finds no file, so that branch never runs. No semver-compatible fix exists: the fix is minimatch 11.0.1, which removes matchOne(), and typedoc's glob() calls it (dist/node-utils.js:328). Re-check when typedoc or typedoc-plugin-markdown is bumped or another package in the site lockfile starts to depend on minimatch, and drop this statement once typedoc requires minimatch 11.

vulnerability.name: GHSA-r3h5-4585-7x3w
vulnerability.description: astro: the `/_image` endpoint used by the @astrojs/node adapter compares paths case-insensitively, so on a case-sensitive filesystem it serves image files from a directory that differs from the output directory only by letter case

statements.impact_statement: astro 7.3.3 is in site/pnpm-lock.yaml only, as the docs site's static-site generator, and nothing in site/ ships in a crate, wheel or npm package. The advisory needs on-demand rendering with the @astrojs/node adapter, whose server answers `/_image` requests. `grep -c '@astrojs/node' site/package.json site/pnpm-lock.yaml` counts 0 in both files, so the adapter is not installed. `grep -nE '\b(output|adapter|prerender)\b' site/astro.config.ts` matches nothing, so the build uses Astro's default static output with no adapter, and `grep -rn prerender site/src site/authored` finds no route that opts out of prerendering. The config sets `image: { service: passthroughImageService() }`, so the site optimizes no images. .github/workflows/docs.yml runs `astro build` and uploads site/dist to GitHub Pages as static files, so no Astro server and no `/_image` endpoint exist where the site is served. Re-check if the site adds @astrojs/node or any other server adapter, sets `output` or a route's `prerender` to on-demand rendering, or is served by `astro preview` or `astro dev` instead of static hosting. Drop this statement and its osv-scanner ignore once astro is 7.4.7 or later.

vulnerability.name: GHSA-mh32-jxcr-mh9f
vulnerability.description: astro: a dynamic tag whose name is a string keeps `/` in the element name, and the MDX JSX renderer does not filter string tag names, so untrusted input used as an element name injects attributes

statements.impact_statement: astro 7.3.3 is in site/pnpm-lock.yaml only, as the docs site's static-site generator. The advisory needs untrusted input (a request parameter, an uncontrolled CMS field) to choose all or part of an element name in a dynamic tag (`const Tag = ...; <Tag />`) or in MDX. The site's own templates are three files, site/src/components/Head.astro, PageActions.astro and PageTitle.astro (`git ls-files site | grep -E '\.(astro|mdx|tsx|jsx)$'`), and `grep -nE '(const|let|var) +[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]* *=' site/src/components/*.astro` finds no capitalized identifier assigned from a string: every capitalized tag in them is an imported component. The same grep over the `.astro` files of the installed dependencies finds one dynamic tag, `HeadingElement` in @astrojs/starlight 0.41.10's components/AnchorHeading.astro, which accepts only heading levels 1 to 6 and which no site source references (`grep -rn AnchorHeading site/src site/authored site/astro.config.ts docs` finds nothing). Content is the repository's own Markdown: docs/ and site/authored/ hold `.md` files and no `.mdx` (`git ls-files docs site/authored | grep -c '\.mdx$'` prints 0), and the reference pages generated beside them at build time are `.md` too. The build is static (no `output`, `adapter` or `prerender` setting in site/astro.config.ts) and no site source reads `Astro.request`, `Astro.url.searchParams`, `Astro.cookies` or `Astro.params`, so no request input exists when a page renders. Re-check if a template or MDX page takes an element name from content, front matter or a request, if the site adds `.mdx` content or content from outside the repository, or if it adds a server adapter or on-demand rendering. Drop this statement and its osv-scanner ignore once astro is 7.4.5 or later.

vulnerability.name: RUSTSEC-2026-0542
vulnerability.description: humantime: marked unmaintained in every version; the advisory names no vulnerable code

statements.impact_statement: RUSTSEC-2026-0542 is an informational advisory (`informational = "unmaintained"`) with no fixed release: it marks every humantime version unmaintained and describes no defect. humantime 2.4.0 is in Cargo.lock only through cucumber 0.23.0, the test runner that agentd, microvms-cli and microvms-core list under `[dev-dependencies]`; `cargo tree -i humantime@2.4.0 -e normal` prints nothing, and `cargo tree -i humantime@2.4.0 --depth 2` lists cucumber alone. No build dependency or shipped binary, wheel or npm package links it, and crates/agentd/fuzz/Cargo.lock has no humantime (`grep -c 'name = "humantime"' crates/agentd/fuzz/Cargo.lock` prints 0). cucumber calls only `humantime::parse_duration`, on the test runner's `--retry-after` command-line value and on `@retry(...).after(...)` tags in the repository's own feature files (cucumber 0.23.0 src/runner/basic.rs:84 and :163). cucumber 0.23.0 is its newest release and requires humantime unconditionally, so no update removes it. Re-check when cucumber publishes a release, if `cargo tree -i humantime -e normal` ever prints a dependent, or if RustSec files a vulnerability against humantime. Drop this statement and the osv-scanner ignore once Cargo.lock has no humantime or the advisory is withdrawn.
